Mfa.//: The CEILING on platform-operator MFA enforcement, not the enforcement itself — that is a persisted, versioned, audited singleton row (platform.PlatformMfaPolicies). See SECURITY.md. IsolatedTestInfrastructure set true in a Production-classified environment FAILS STARTUP; a value outside a documented range throws rather than being clamped.
Mfa.// BrowserTrustHours: SEED ONLY, range 8–720. It is what 'remember this browser' lasts for until a policy row exists; from then on platform.PlatformMfaPolicies.BrowserTrustHours and .BrowserTrustEnabled decide, and this value is ignored. Change the window on Platform Admin → Security → Platform Authentication, where it is Owner-only, re-authenticated, reasoned and audited — editing it here on a configured deployment changes nothing and looks like it did.

Platform.// DataBoundaries: What THIS deployment's own infrastructure is, per tenant data-boundary type. Deliberately EMPTY here: these are facts about one estate (a Nexora-hosted install's Neon project is not a self-hosted install's database), and a default would make every deployment claim somebody else's. Left empty, provisioning registers nothing and an operator registers each boundary by hand exactly as before. Populate per type — PostgreSqlTenantScope, ObjectStorage, SearchIndex, EmbeddingStore, Cache, QueuePayload, GeneratedExport, AiOcrProvider, Subprocessor — each with OpaqueProviderReference (an opaque id, never a URL or connection string), Region (must equal every tenant's contractual DataRegion or registration is refused), BackupPolicyReference and a positive BackupPolicyVersion; Classification, Disposition and LogicalKey are optional per-type overrides. A type declared with a field missing is REFUSED and stays on the manual path rather than being defaulted. Only PostgreSqlTenantScope is verified, from a recorded probe of the running database; the rest are registered, which is what deletion certification needs and is not a claim that anything about them was checked.

Email.//MaxNewMessagesPerMailboxAttempt: Bounded oldest-first backlog drain. Deferred mail stays on the server and the recovery checkpoint does not advance until the window is empty.
Email.//MailboxAttemptTimeoutSeconds: Total budget for one mailbox. Expiry is recorded as a transient failure and the next mailbox is attempted without advancing the success checkpoint.
Email.//NetworkOperationTimeoutSeconds: Maximum time for each IMAP connect, authenticate, open, search, fetch, acknowledge, or disconnect operation.

Assembly.//StrandedComponentSweepMinutes: How long a part of an email may sit non-terminal before the recovery sweep resolves it from the actual state of its extraction job. Age only decides what is LOOKED at: a job with attempts left is always left alone, so this is not a timeout on live work. 30 minutes comfortably clears the queue's exponential backoff (capped at one hour per attempt) for everything but a job on its last, longest wait.

Ollama.//MaxOutputTokens: num_predict per call. Was UNSET, which silently meant 4096 and capped extraction at ~5 line items per chunk. 8192 is the largest value we have observed this model complete within the 180s client timeout (measured live 2026-08-05); the provider itself allows up to 65536. Raise it only alongside a measured generation-throughput number, or the truncation outage becomes a timeout outage.
